pr_title: fix: prevent StackOverflow, IndexOutOfRange, and InvalidCast crashes on malformed JavaScript
issue:
#### Issue #2349: BigInt exponentiation bypasses all execution constraints (LimitMemory, TimeoutInterval, MaxStatements)

**Version/platform/runtime used**
- Jint 4.6.3 (NuGet, latest stable)
- Also verified on current main branch (commit 5e8f6f3, post-#2340 fix)
- .NET 10.0, Linux x64

**Describe the bug**

A 15-byte JavaScript input containing BigInt exponentiation (`11n**711111111n`) bypasses all execution constraints, causing the process to allocate ~8 GB of memory and hang indefinitely at 100% CPU.

**Reproduction**

```csharp
var engine = new Engine(options =>
{
    options.TimeoutInterval(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
    options.LimitRecursion(100);
    options.MaxStatements(10_000);
    options.LimitMemory(16_000_000); // 16 MB
});

// Hangs forever at ~8 GB memory and 100% CPU, despite all limits
engine.Execute("11n**711111111n");
```

**Observed behavior**

The process allocates ~8 GB of memory and enters an infinite loop, consuming 100% CPU indefinitely. The `LimitMemory(16_000_000)` constraint has no effect. The process never throws a `MemoryLimitExceededException`, `TimeoutException`, or any other exception - it hangs forever and must be killed externally.

No stack trace is available because the process never terminates on its own.

**Expected behavior**

The engine should throw a `MemoryLimitExceededException` when the configured memory limit is exceeded, or a `TimeoutException` / `StatementsCountOverflowException` if execution takes too long.

**Impact**

Any application that executes untrusted JavaScript with Jint is vulnerable to denial of service. The standard mitigations (`LimitMemory`, `TimeoutInterval`, `MaxStatements`) do not protect against this input. A single 15-byte request causes the process to hang indefinitely at ~8 GB memory and 100% CPU.

Note: This is a separate issue from the crashes fixed in #2340. Those fixes addressed StackOverflow, IndexOutOfRange, and InvalidCast. This OOM issue persists on current main.

**Root cause**

The input `11n**711111111n` is a single statement — BigInt exponentiation computing 11^711,111,111. This calls `BigInteger.Pow(11, 711_111_111)` in `JintBinaryExpression.cs`, which attempts to produce a number with ~700 million digits.

All three execution constraints fail because they are checked at **statement boundaries** only (`RunBeforeExecuteStatementChecks` in `JintStatement.Execute`), not during expression evaluation. `BigInteger.Pow` is a single blocking .NET call that runs inside a single statement — `LimitMemory` never gets to compare allocations, `TimeoutInterval`'s CancellationToken is never inspected, and `MaxStatements` counts only 1 statement.

A possible fix would be to validate the BigInt exponent magnitude before calling `BigInteger.Pow`, or to add constraint checks inside expensive expression operations.

**Security consideration**

This issue may warrant a security advisory (GHSA). The combination of a small payload (15 bytes), uncatchable failure mode (OOM kill, not an exception), and bypass of the intended mitigation (`LimitMemory`) makes this exploitable as a denial-of-service attack against any application executing untrusted JavaScript with Jint.

**Additional context**

Discovered through coverage-guided fuzzing with AFL++ and SharpFuzz.

pr_title: Add configurable animation timing functions with Material Design easing
issue:
#### Issue #11638: Revise animations

### Describe your idea

Currently the snackbar uses a slow linear animation:

https://github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor/blob/b8c6088926e33d95d0b79f17ce54d5a801e9d147/src/MudBlazor/Components/Snackbar/SnackBarMessageState.cs#L47

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/587cd592-d5a3-4dd5-83cb-02cbd35edac9

But we could ease it (and speed it up by default):

`opacity: {0}; animation: {1}ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) {2};`

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/182da220-97e6-4eea-96d2-8f87237e507c

And speed up popover transitions (date picker fade is noticeably slow)

### Alternatives and examples

- https://mui.com/material-ui/react-snackbar/
- https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/transitions/transition-patterns
- https://github.com/material-components/material-components-web/blob/6ceadb81df508ac08ab007c52c4d3dc1d811cc15/packages/mdc-animation/_animation.scss
- https://m2.material.io/develop/web/supporting/animation
- https://m2.material.io/design/motion/understanding-motion.html#principles
- https://m2.material.io/design/motion/customization.html#oscillation

Revise the animations in the entire library to use Material Design 2 styles, with the ability to change them in the theme so they can follow Material Design 3 when we implement that if there are any differences.

pr_title: Remove stale K8s references from runtime/types.py
issue:
#### Issue #3811: [iris] Clean up k8s references in runtime/types.py after kubernetes runtime removal

After removing lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/runtime/kubernetes.py (see #3810),
the MountKind comments and ContainerPhase.PENDING docstring in runtime/types.py
will have stale K8s references (e.g. "emptyDir on K8s", "K8s pod scheduling").

Once the kubernetes runtime is removed, update comments in types.py that reference K8s as
a ContainerRuntime implementation to only refer to Docker/process runtimes.

Note: runtime/entrypoint.py has no k8s-specific code; only types.py needs attention.

pr_title: Add VB.NET test coverage and code fix support for MSTest analyzers
issue:
#### Issue #4031: Analyzers don't have test coverage for VB, and codefixes are implemented only for C#

## Summary

<!--
Brief summary of what this proposal is about.
-->

Currently, our analyzers are implemented both for C# and VB, but the tests are only validating C#.

And the codefixes are only implemented for C#, not implemented for VB at all.

## Background and Motivation

<!--
What is the problem you are solving and in what context did you encounter it?
-->

## Proposed Feature

<!--
Please provide a sketch of the feature you are proposing. Be as specific as you can: the more specific the proposal, the easier the process will be. Including screenshots of some of the existing problems can also help a lot here.
-->

## Alternative Designs

<!--
Were there other options you considered?
How does this compare to features in other editors?
-->

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+# VB.NET Support Implementation Guide
+
+This document outlines the changes made to add VB.NET support to MSTest analyzers and provides guidance for extending this support to remaining code fix providers.
+
+## What Was Implemented
+
+### 1. VB Test Infrastructure
+- Created `VisualBasicCodeFixVerifier<TAnalyzer, TCodeFix>` infrastructure
+- Added `VisualBasicVerifierHelper` for VB-specific compiler settings
+- Established pattern for VB test case creation
+
+### 2. VB Code Fix Provider Support
+The following code fix providers have been updated to support VB.NET:
+
+- ✅ **TestContextShouldBeValidFixer** - Complete rewrite using language-agnostic APIs
+- ✅ **AssemblyInitializeShouldBeValidFixer** - Added VB language support
+- ✅ **UseAttributeOnTestMethodFixer** - Added VB language support  
+- ✅ **TestClassShouldBeValidFixer** - Added VB language support
+
+### 3. VB Test Coverage Added
+- **TestContextShouldBeValidAnalyzer** - 4 comprehensive VB tests
+- **TestMethodShouldBeValidAnalyzer** - 3 VB tests  
+- **TestClassShouldBeValidAnalyzer** - 3 VB tests
+
+## Remaining Work
+
+### Code Fix Providers Still Needing VB Support
+The following 19 code fix providers still only support C# and need to be updated:
+
+1. AddTestClassFixer.cs
+2. AssemblyCleanupShouldBeValidFixer.cs
+3. AssertionArgsShouldAvoidConditionalAccessFixer.cs
+4. AssertionArgsShouldBePassedInCorrectOrderFixer.cs
+5. AvoidAssertAreSameWithValueTypesFixer.cs
+6. AvoidExpectedExceptionAttributeFixer.cs
+7. ClassCleanupShouldBeValidFixer.cs
+8. ClassInitializeShouldBeValidFixer.cs
+9. PreferAssertFailOverAlwaysFalseConditionsFixer.cs
+10. PreferConstructorOverTestInitializeFixer.cs
+11. PreferDisposeOverTestCleanupFixer.cs
+12. PreferTestCleanupOverDisposeFixer.cs
+13. PreferTestInitializeOverConstructorFixer.cs
+14. PublicMethodShouldBeTestMethodFixer.cs
+15. TestCleanupShouldBeValidFixer.cs
+16. TestInitializeShouldBeValidFixer.cs
+17. TestMethodShouldBeValidCodeFix.cs
+18. UseNewerAssertThrowsFixer.cs
+19. UseProperAssertMethodsFixer.cs
+
+### How to Add VB Support to Code Fix Providers
+
+#### Simple Cases (Attribute-based fixes using DocumentEditor)
+For code fix providers that already use `DocumentEditor` or simple attribute additions:
+
+1. Update the `ExportCodeFixProvider` attribute:
+```csharp
+// From:
+[ExportCodeFixProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp, Name = nameof(MyFixer))]
+
+// To:
+[ExportCodeFixProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp, LanguageNames.VisualBasic, Name = nameof(MyFixer))]
+```
+
+#### Complex Cases (Syntax-specific operations)
+For code fix providers using C#-specific syntax trees (like most remaining ones):
+
+1. Remove C#-specific using statements:
+```csharp
+// Remove these:
+using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp;
+using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Syntax;
+```
+
+2. Replace C#-specific syntax operations with language-agnostic alternatives:
+```csharp
+// Instead of C#-specific syntax operations, use:
+DocumentEditor editor = await DocumentEditor.CreateAsync(document, cancellationToken);
+SyntaxGenerator generator = editor.Generator;
+
+// Use generator methods for creating syntax nodes:
+var propertyDeclaration = generator.PropertyDeclaration(
+    name: "PropertyName",
+    type: generator.TypeExpression(typeSymbol),
+    accessibility: Accessibility.Public,
+    getAccessorStatements: null, // Auto-property
+    setAccessorStatements: null);
+```
+
+3. Follow the pattern established in `TestContextShouldBeValidFixer` for language-agnostic implementation.
+
+### Adding VB Test Coverage
+
+For each analyzer test file:
+
+1. Add VB verifier import:
+```csharp
+using VerifyVB = MSTest.Analyzers.Test.VisualBasicCodeFixVerifier<
+    MSTest.Analyzers.YourAnalyzer,
+    MSTest.Analyzers.YourFixer>;
+```
+
+2. Add VB test methods covering key scenarios:
+```csharp
+[TestMethod]
+public async Task WhenCondition_VB_ExpectedResult()
+{
+    string code = """
+        Imports Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting
+        
+        <TestClass>
+        Public Class MyTestClass
+            ' VB.NET test code here
+        End Class
+        """;
+        
+    await VerifyVB.VerifyAnalyzerAsync(code, /* expected diagnostics */);
+}
+```
+
+## VB.NET Syntax Reference
+
+Key VB.NET syntax differences for test cases:
+
+- **Imports** instead of `using`
+- **Attributes**: `<TestClass>`, `<TestMethod>` 
+- **Classes**: `Public Class MyClass ... End Class`
+- **Methods**: `Public Sub MyMethod() ... End Sub`
+- **Properties**: `Public Property MyProp As String`
+- **Static**: `Shared` instead of `static`
+- **Modules**: `Public Module MyModule ... End Module` (equivalent to static class)
+- **Comments**: `'` instead of `//`
+
+## Benefits of This Implementation

pr_title: Add GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows for Windows and macOS builds
issue:
#### Issue #419: GitHub actions CI/CD integration for Windows and MacOS

We need CI/CD integration using GitHub actions, for this the engine codebase has a script in the Scripts folder called build_razix.py, we won't be testing engine as we need a RTX capable GPUs and only we will support building on Windows and MacOS for now, so we can have a gihub workflow to build the engine using this script only for GoldMaster builds... we can extend this to linux in future once support is added and NO tests. Also we need badges in the readme showing build status.

The build is made before we merge the PR and every time a new commit is added to master like when a PR is merged

Commits with tags that are merged into master can have artifacts build and release as a release.

We can also bi-weekly builds on mater to check for stability.

+name: Release Build
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - 'v*.*.*'
+
+jobs:
+  create-release:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    outputs:
+      upload_url: ${{ steps.create_release.outputs.upload_url }}
+      release_id: ${{ steps.create_release.outputs.id }}
+    steps:
+    - name: Create Release
+      id: create_release
+      uses: actions/create-release@v1
+      env:
+        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+      with:
+        tag_name: ${{ github.ref }}
+        release_name: Razix Engine ${{ github.ref }}
+        body: |
+          Razix Engine Release ${{ github.ref }}
+          
+          ## Build Artifacts
+          - Windows (GoldMaster): razix-windows-goldmaster.zip
+          - macOS (GoldMaster): razix-macos-goldmaster.zip
+          
+          ## Changes
+          See the commit history for detailed changes in this release.
+        draft: false
+        prerelease: false
+
+  build-windows:
+    needs: create-release
+    runs-on: windows-latest
+    
+    steps:
+    - name: Checkout repository
+      uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      with:
+        submodules: recursive
+    
+    - name: Setup Python
+      uses: actions/setup-python@v4
+      with:
+        python-version: '3.x'
+    
+    - name: Setup MSBuild
+      uses: microsoft/setup-msbuild@v1.3
+    
+    - name: Generate Project Files
+      run: |
+        cd Scripts
+        .\GenerateVS22.bat
+      shell: cmd
+    
+    - name: Build Engine (GoldMaster)
+      run: |
+        python Scripts/build_razix.py --platform windows --config GoldMaster
+      shell: cmd
+    
+    - name: Package Windows Build
+      run: |
+        7z a razix-windows-goldmaster.zip bin/GoldMaster-windows-x64/**/*
+      shell: cmd
+    
+    - name: Upload Windows Release Asset

+        asset_name: razix-windows-goldmaster.zip
+        asset_content_type: application/zip
+
+  build-macos:

+    - name: Setup Python

pr_title: Fix spurious error when checking out a PR with untracked files and add "never show again" option
issue: #### Issue #7294: Spurious error when checking out a PR with untracked files - Extension version: 0.114.0 - VSCode Version: 1.102.0 (cb0c47c0cfaad0757385834bd89d410c78a856c0) - OS: Windows 11 Pro (24H2) - Repository Clone Configuration (single repository/fork of an upstream repository): NA - GitHub Product (GitHub.com/GitHub Enterprise version x.x.x): NA Steps to Reproduce: 1. Have untracked files in your workspace 2. Try to check out a PR branch 3. The above warning pops up: "You have uncommitted changes that would be overwritten by checking out this pull request. Choose how to handle your uncommitted changes before checking out the pull request." I can see a use case for the warning especially for novice users, but it seems like it triggers even on spurious cases (e.g. above). In the case of untracked files, unless the PR branch happens to create and commit a file at the same path, this warning should not show up. For my use case, I switch between a ton of different environment files/configuration constantly, and work on multiple features at the same time, and so have a lot of untracked files in my workspace. It would be good if at the very least, we can disable this popup with a workspace setting, or just remove the warning entirely for untracked files. This will allow the warning to still show up in legitimate conflict cases (instead of simply showing an error toast + manual resolution, as is the case in previous versions).

pr_title: fix: token expiration
issue:
#### Issue #30: Fix: Token auto-refresh fails due to incorrect 'expires_in' value

The Spotify access token expires after 1 hour, but the MCP-server is currently configured to treat it as valid for 30 days. 
This prevents the `@spotify/web-api-ts-sdk` from automatically refreshing the token when it actually expires, 
leading to authentication errors after the first hour of usage.

Suggested Fix Change :
expires_in back to 3600 (1 hour) to match Spotify's actual token lifespan. 
This will allow the SDK to correctly identify when the token is about to expire and use the refresh_token to fetch a new one.

#### Issue #5465: Security: 34 stale Dependabot alerts on removed langwatch_nlp/uv.lock manifest (needs dismissal or re-scan)

## Summary

34 open Dependabot alerts (8 high, 16 moderate, 10 low) are all reported against the manifest path `langwatch_nlp/uv.lock`, which no longer exists in the repository. They are stale and cannot be fixed by a code change.

## Root cause

The Python `langwatch_nlp/` service was replaced by the Go `nlpgo` engine. `Dockerfile.langwatch_nlp` states it directly:

> nlpgo is the sole NLP engine ... No uvicorn, no langwatch_nlp [Python]

The `langwatch_nlp/` source directory, including its `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, was removed. Confirmed at `main`:

- `langwatch_nlp/uv.lock` returns 404 via the contents API
- `git ls-tree -r origin/main` finds no `langwatch_nlp/` source tree, only `Dockerfile.langwatch_nlp` and the Helm chart templates that reference the running service
- there is no `uv.lock` or `pyproject.toml` anywhere under `langwatch/`

Because the manifest is gone, there is nothing to bump. Dependabot has not re-scanned these away on its own.

## Affected packages (all on `langwatch_nlp/uv.lock`)

- aiohttp: #1384 #1383 #1382 #1381 #1380 #1379 #1378 #1377 #1376 #1251 #1247
- pyjwt / PyJWT: #1375 #1374 #1373 #1372 #1371
- starlette / Starlette: #1396 #1395 #1387 #1386 #1261
- python-multipart: #1393 #1392 #1391 #1390
- tornado: #1394 #1389 #1388 #1300
- cryptography: #1385
- transformers: #1552
- python-liquid: #1527
- diskcache: #404
- idna: #1188

## Recommended action (human decision)

These are advisory-only from the security-triage agent, which cannot dismiss alerts. Either:

1. Bulk-dismiss the 34 alerts as "no longer in use" (the vulnerable code path was deleted with the Python service), or
2. Trigger a Dependabot re-scan of the repository so it drops manifests that no longer exist.

The Go `nlpgo` engine that replaced this service is tracked under its own Go module manifests and is unaffected by this issue.

#### Issue #575: Workflow: fake-strategist-task.yaml prompt diverged from TaskSpawner after PR #556 merge

🤖 **Kelos Agent** @gjkim42

## Area: Task Template Maintenance

## Summary

PR #556 (merged 2026-03-06) made substantive prompt changes to `kelos-fake-strategist.yaml` — removing the "Workflow Improvements" focus area, widening the dedup search window, and adding cross-agent boundaries. These changes were **not propagated** to `self-development/tasks/fake-strategist-task.yaml`, creating significant prompt drift that affects manual strategist runs via the `run-fake-strategist.yaml` workflow.

The open PR #551 (which addresses issue #544 about task template drift) only covers cosmetic changes identified *before* #556 merged — it does not include these newer, more impactful divergences.

## Findings

### 1. "Workflow Improvements" focus area still present in task template (removed from TaskSpawner)

PR #556 deliberately removed focus area #2 ("Workflow Improvements") from `kelos-fake-strategist.yaml` to reduce inter-agent overlap — this area is handled by `kelos-self-update` and `kelos-config-update`. The TaskSpawner now has 3 focus areas.

**TaskSpawner** (`kelos-fake-strategist.yaml`, lines 39-55) — 3 focus areas:
1. New Use Cases
2. Integration Opportunities
3. New CRDs & API Extensions

**Task template** (`tasks/fake-strategist-task.yaml`, lines 34-58) — still has 4 focus areas:
1. New Use Cases
2. **Workflow Improvements** ← removed from TaskSpawner
3. Integration Opportunities
4. New CRDs & API Extensions

**Impact:** Manual strategist runs via `run-fake-strategist.yaml` may choose "Workflow Improvements" as their focus area, producing issues that overlap with `kelos-self-update` and `kelos-config-update` output — exactly the problem #556 was designed to prevent.

### 2. Dedup search window not widened in task template

PR #556 changed the dedup search from `--limit 10` to `--limit 50 --json number,title` across all cron agents.

**TaskSpawner** (`kelos-fake-strategist.yaml`, line 70):
```
gh issue list --label generated-by-kelos --state open --limit 50 --json number,title
```

**Task template** (`tasks/fake-strategist-task.yaml`, line 71):
```
gh issue list --label generated-by-kelos --limit 10
```

**Impact:** Manual strategist runs only check the 10 most recent issues for duplicates, missing 40+ existing issues. With 40+ open `generated-by-kelos` issues, this makes duplicate creation likely.

### 3. Cross-agent awareness constraints missing from task template

PR #556 added explicit cross-agent boundaries to the TaskSpawner (lines 71-74):
```
- The following areas are handled by other agents — do not create issues about them:
  - Self-development workflow improvements, prompt tuning, config alignment → kelos-self-update
  - Documentation, CLI UX, error messages → kelos-fake-user
  - Agent configuration based on PR reviews → kelos-config-update
```

The task template has **none** of these constraints (lines 66-72). Manual runs lack any awareness of other agents' responsibilities.

### 4. "Exit without output" constraint missing from task template

The TaskSpawner includes (line 75):
```
- If after reviewing existing issues you cannot identify something genuinely new and actionable, exit without creating an issue or PR. Not every run needs to produce output
```

The task template only says (line 72):
```
- If after reviewing existing issues you cannot identify something genuinely new and actionable, exit without creating an issue or PR. Not every run needs to produce output
```

Wait — actually the task template does have a similar line. Let me check... The task template's version (line 72) is weaker:
```
- If after reviewing existing issues you cannot identify something genuinely new and actionable, exit without creating an issue or PR. Not every run needs to produce output
```

This line was present before #556 but is equivalent. No gap here — correction: this finding is not applicable.

## Proposed Changes

### Sync `fake-strategist-task.yaml` prompt with `kelos-fake-strategist.yaml`

Replace the task template's prompt section (lines 29-72) with the current TaskSpawner prompt content. Specifically:

1. **Remove focus area #2** ("Workflow Improvements") — lines 42-46
2. **Renumber remaining focus areas** — current #3 becomes #2, #4 becomes #3
3. **Update dedup search** — replace `--limit 10` with `--state open --limit 50 --json number,title` (line 71)
4. **Add cross-agent awareness** — add the "areas handled by other agents" constraint block
5. **Add backtick fencing** around `gh issue create` command (PR #551 already proposes this)

### Update PR #551 or create a new PR

Since PR #551 is still open and addresses #544, the simplest approach is to update #551 to include these additional sync changes. Alternatively, a new PR can address the #556-related drift separately.

## Relationship to existing issues

| Issue/PR | What it covers | What it doesn't cover |
|----------|---------------|----------------------|
| #544 (open issue) | General task template drift problem | Not aware of #556 changes |
| #551 (open PR, fixes #544) | Backtick fencing, YAML quoting, README docs | Does not sync #556 prompt changes (focus area removal, dedup widening, cross-agent constraints) |
| #553 (closed issue) | Cross-spawner dedup widening | Only covered TaskSpawner files, not task templates |

This issue specifically tracks the **new drift introduced by #556** that is not covered by the existing #544/#551 pair.

## Evidence

- PR #556 diff: removed "Workflow Improvements" from `kelos-fake-strategist.yaml`, widened dedup to `--limit 50`, added cross-agent constraints
- Current `tasks/fake-strategist-task.yaml` on main: still contains all 4 focus areas, `--limit 10`, no cross-agent constraints
- `run-fake-strategist.yaml` workflow: directly applies `tasks/fake-strategist-task.yaml`, meaning manual runs use the outdated prompt

/kind cleanup

#### Issue #911: API: Add persistent execution mode to TaskSpawner for warm agent sessions that eliminate per-task cold-start overhead

🤖 **Kelos Strategist Agent** @gjkim42

## Area: New CRDs & API Extensions

## Summary

Every Kelos Task currently creates a fresh Kubernetes Job with 3–8 sequential init containers (git clone, remote setup, branch setup, file injection, plugin installation) before the agent even starts. For short-lived tasks like triage (~30–60s of actual agent work), this cold-start overhead often exceeds the productive work time. This proposal adds a **persistent execution mode** to TaskSpawner that keeps agent pods running between tasks, maintaining the workspace and agent context across work items — eliminating per-task pod scheduling, git cloning, and agent initialization overhead.

This is architecturally distinct from all existing proposals: it changes the execution model from "one-pod-per-task" to "warm-agent-handles-multiple-tasks," and it compounds the benefits of workspace caching (#774), history context (#792), and concurrency control (#675) by making them implicit rather than requiring extra infrastructure per invocation.

## Problem

### 1. The cold-start tax is measured in minutes, not seconds

Every Task follows the same startup sequence in `job_builder.go` (lines 360–660):

| Init Container | Purpose | Typical Duration |
|---|---|---|
| `git-clone` | `git clone --depth 1 --no-single-branch` into EmptyDir | 5–30s (varies by repo size) |
| `remote-setup` | Add upstream/fork remotes | 2–5s |
| `branch-setup` | Fetch + checkout or create branch | 2–5s |
| `file-injection` | Write `workspace.spec.files[]` into repo | 1–2s |
| `plugin-setup` | Install AgentConfig plugins/skills | 5–30s (downloads npm packages) |
| `agentconfig-setup` | Write CLAUDE.md, MCP server configs | 2–5s |

Plus Kubernetes overhead:
- Pod scheduling: 1–5s
- Image pull (if not cached): 30–120s
- Agent process startup (Claude Code initialization, codebase indexing): 5–15s

**Total per task: 20–120+ seconds before any useful work begins.**

The workspace volume is always an `EmptyDir` (`job_builder.go:371-374`):
```go
volume := corev1.Volume{
    Name: WorkspaceVolumeName,
    VolumeSource: corev1.VolumeSource{
        EmptyDir: &corev1.EmptyDirVolumeSource{},
    },
}
```

This means every task clones the repo from scratch — even if the previous task on the same spawner cloned the exact same repo 30 seconds ago.

### 2. Short-lived tasks are disproportionately affected

The self-development deployment illustrates the problem. The `kelos-triage` spawner (`self-development/kelos-triage.yaml`) has `maxConcurrency: 8` and `pollInterval: 1m`. Triage tasks are lightweight — the agent reads one issue, checks for duplicates via `gh issue list`, posts a comment, and adds labels. Actual agent work: 30–60 seconds. But each triage task pays the full cold-start penalty.

At 20 triage tasks/day with 60s average cold start, that's **20 minutes/day of infrastructure overhead** for work that takes ~15 minutes of actual agent time. The cold-start-to-work ratio approaches 1:1.

Other short-lived patterns with the same problem:
- `kelos-squash-commits`: runs `git rebase`, takes <30s of agent time
- `kelos-reviewer`: reads a diff, posts a comment, ~60s of agent time
- `kelos-planner`: reads an issue, posts a plan comment, ~60–120s of agent time

### 3. Agent context is lost between tasks — expensive to rebuild

AI agents need to understand the codebase to do useful work. Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, scans directory structure, and builds a mental model of the project. This context loading happens every time because each task starts a fresh process.

For Kelos's own development, every agent independently:
- Reads `CLAUDE.md` + `self-development/README.md`
- Scans the project structure
- Understands the CRD types, controllers, and conventions

This codebase context is identical across all tasks from the same spawner, yet it's rebuilt from scratch every time — consuming API tokens to re-read the same files.

### 4. Industry trend: persistent agent sessions are becoming standard

The AI coding agent ecosystem is moving toward persistent sessions:
- **Claude Code** supports conversation resume and persistent memory in `~/.claude/`
- **Cursor** maintains background agents with persistent state
- **Devin** runs as a persistent session that handles multiple requests
- **GitHub Copilot Workspace** maintains session state across interactions

Kelos's one-shot execution model is architecturally sound for safety and isolation, but the overhead makes it impractical for high-frequency, low-latency workflows where the same agent processes many similar items from the same source.

## Proposed API Changes

### Add `executionMode` and `sessionConfig` to TaskSpawnerSpec

```go
type TaskSpawnerSpec struct {
    // ... existing fields ...

    // ExecutionMode controls how agent pods are managed.
    // "ephemeral" (default): one Job per Task, pod is deleted after completion.
    // "persistent": agents run in long-lived pods that handle multiple Tasks
    //   sequentially, maintaining workspace and process state between items.
    // +optional
    // +kubebuilder:default=ephemeral
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Enum=ephemeral;persistent
    ExecutionMode ExecutionMode `json:"executionMode,omitempty"`

    // SessionConfig configures persistent execution mode behavior.
    // Ignored when executionMode is "ephemeral".
    // +optional
    SessionConfig *SessionConfig `json:"sessionConfig,omitempty"`
}

type ExecutionMode string

const (
    ExecutionModeEphemeral  ExecutionMode = "ephemeral"
    ExecutionModePersistent ExecutionMode = "persistent"
)

type SessionConfig struct {
    // IdleTimeout is the duration after which an idle agent pod is terminated.
    // The pod restarts when new work items arrive.
    // Defaults to "30m".
    // +optional
    IdleTimeout *metav1.Duration `json:"idleTimeout,omitempty"`

    // MaxTasksPerSession is the maximum number of tasks an agent pod handles
    // before being restarted. This prevents unbounded memory growth and
    // ensures periodic workspace cleanup.
    // Defaults to 0 (unlimited).
    // +optional
    MaxTasksPerSession *int32 `json:"maxTasksPerSession,omitempty"`

    // MaxSessionDuration is the maximum lifetime of an agent pod regardless
    // of activity. Ensures periodic fresh starts.
    // Defaults to "8h".
    // +optional
    MaxSessionDuration *metav1.Duration `json:"maxSessionDuration,omitempty"`

    // WorkspaceReset controls how the workspace is cleaned between tasks.
    // +optional
    WorkspaceReset *WorkspaceResetPolicy `json:"workspaceReset,omitempty"`

    // Replicas is the number of persistent agent pods to maintain.
    // Work items are distributed across available replicas.
    // Defaults to 1.
    // +optional
    Replicas *int32 `json:"replicas,omitempty"`
}

type WorkspaceResetPolicy struct {
    // Git resets the workspace to a clean state between tasks.
    // Runs: git checkout <ref>, git clean -fdx, git pull
    // Defaults to true.
    // +optional
    Git *bool `json:"git,omitempty"`

    // PreserveDirectories lists directories to preserve across resets
    // (e.g., "node_modules", ".venv", ".cache"). These survive git clean.
    // +optional
    PreserveDirectories []string `json:"preserveDirectories,omitempty"`
}
```

### New Task Phase: `Queued`

```go
// TaskPhaseQueued means the Task has been created but is waiting
// for an available persistent agent session to process it.
TaskPhaseQueued TaskPhase = "Queued"
```

Phase flow with persistent mode:
```
Queued → Running → Succeeded/Failed
```

vs. ephemeral mode (unchanged):
```
Pending → [Waiting] → Running → Succeeded/Failed
```

## Architecture

### Ephemeral mode (current — unchanged)
```
TaskSpawner discovers item
  → Creates Task resource
    → Task Controller creates Job (1 Pod with init containers)
      → Init: git-clone, remote-setup, branch-setup, plugins...
      → Agent container runs prompt
      → Pod terminates
    → Task marked Succeeded/Failed
```

#### Issue #1406: Configuration Alignment: retriage replaced Agora issue slots before pickup

🤖 **Kelos Agent** @gjkim42

<!-- kelos-taskspawner=agora-self-update -->

## Area

Configuration Alignment

## Problem

Agora's generated issue lifecycle bypasses triage, and the single-slot update
mechanism can preserve stale classifications when an agent replaces one
candidate with a different one.

Evidence from `self-development/agora/`:

- `agora-fake-user.yaml` and `agora-fake-strategist.yaml` create and update
  their issue slots with only `generated-by-kelos` and `triage-accepted`.
- Slot replacement uses `gh issue edit`, which changes the title and body but
  preserves any existing `kind/*`, `priority/*`, and `actor/*` labels.
- `agora-triage.yaml` reacts only to `opened` issues without
  `triage-accepted`, or `reopened` issues with `needs-actor`. An in-place slot
  edit cannot receive fresh triage.
- `agora-workers.yaml` and `agora-pr-responder.yaml` also tell agents to create
  follow-up issues with only `generated-by-kelos` and `triage-accepted`.
- `agora-workers.yaml` accepts `/kelos pick-up` on any open issue from the
  maintainer. It neither requires `actor/kelos` nor excludes `actor/human`, and
  its prompt has no label guard before implementation.
- `README.md` says `agora-triage` applies the kind, priority, actor, and
  lifecycle labels, which does not match the producer prompts.

Evidence from recent Agora agent activity:

- Agora issue #5 was reused across materially different candidates:
  `Bridge GitHub Actions CI and reviews into Agora inboxes` became
  `Add a GitHub Actions bridge for CI and review events`, then
  `Browser UI cannot authenticate to token-protected servers`, and finally
  `Token-protected deployments break the browser UI and health checks`.
- Agora issue #8 similarly changed from a GitHub Actions reporter proposal to
  recipient-scoped inbox status, then bounded-feed behavior, then back to
  recipient-scoped status.
- Both current open slots, #5 and #8, still have exactly
  `generated-by-kelos` and `triage-accepted`; neither has a kind, priority, or
  actor label.
- Issue #8 proposes new API response fields, a status endpoint, a JSONL record
  kind, CLI behavior, browser behavior, and reporting-skill changes. The
  `agora-triage` prompt classifies those public-contract changes as `kind/api`
  and requires `actor/human`, but the slot never reaches that decision.
- The only merged generated PR, Agora #7, was picked up from actorless issue #4.
  This confirms that the worker path currently proceeds without the actor
  classification.

The current issue-slot model therefore has two failure modes: a new generated
issue is accepted before it is classified, and an in-place replacement can
retain a classification for an unrelated former candidate. A worker-only gate
would stop unsafe pickup but leave generated issues permanently actorless; an
initial-creation-only fix would still leave replacement candidates with stale
labels.

## Proposed Improvement

Route every generated candidate through fresh triage and enforce the resulting
actor decision at pickup.

1. Update `agora-fake-user.yaml` and `agora-fake-strategist.yaml`:
   - Create a new slot with `generated-by-kelos`, `needs-triage`, `needs-kind`,
     `needs-priority`, and `needs-actor`, without `triage-accepted`.
   - When a clearly stronger candidate replaces an unassigned slot, close the
     old issue as superseded and create a fresh issue with the same slot marker
     and unresolved lifecycle labels instead of editing the old title/body.
     The existing `opened` triage trigger can then classify the replacement
     without adding another webhook path.
   - Keep the assigned-slot behavior unchanged.
2. Update follow-up issue instructions in `agora-workers.yaml` and
   `agora-pr-responder.yaml` to use the same unresolved lifecycle labels rather
   than pre-applying `triage-accepted`.
3. Gate `agora-workers.yaml` on the triage result:
   - Require `triage-accepted` and `actor/kelos` in the webhook filter where
     supported, and exclude `actor/human`.
   - After refreshing the issue, re-read its current labels and exit before
     code changes if `actor/kelos` is absent or `actor/human` is present. This
     protects against stale webhook payloads and later label changes.
4. Update `README.md` so slot rotation, generated follow-up triage, and the
   worker actor gate match the actual prompts.

This keeps the change focused on the existing label lifecycle. It does not
change candidate selection, add a new agent, or expand the triage taxonomy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A newly created fake-user, fake-strategist, worker-follow-up, or
  PR-responder-follow-up issue is eligible for `agora-triage` and is not born
  with bare `triage-accepted`.
- Replacing an unassigned discovery candidate produces a fresh open issue and
  closes the superseded slot, leaving at most one open slot for that
  TaskSpawner.
- Replacement candidates cannot inherit the prior issue's kind, priority, or
  actor decision.
- `agora-workers` does not spawn or implement for an issue without
  `actor/kelos`, or for an issue carrying `actor/human`.
- The README describes the same generated-issue and pickup lifecycle as the
  TaskSpawner prompts.

+import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest'
+import { runPreflight } from '../../src/core/preflight'
+import * as fs from 'fs'
+import * as path from 'path'
+import * as os from 'os'
+
+describe('Preflight - Output Formatter', () => {
+  let tempDir: string
+  let configPath: string
+  let originalCwd: string
+
+  beforeEach(() => {
+    originalCwd = process.cwd()
+    tempDir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'preflight-outfmt-'))
+    process.chdir(tempDir)
+    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(tempDir, '.git'))
+    configPath = path.join(tempDir, 'config.yaml')
+  })
+
+  afterEach(() => {
+    process.chdir(originalCwd)
+    fs.rmSync(tempDir, { recursive: true, force: true })
+  })
+
+  it('should use CLI output formatter over config', async () => {
+    fs.writeFileSync(configPath, 'output_formatter: cat\n')
+    const result = await runPreflight(
+      ['node', 'claude-composer', '--output-formatter', 'jq'],
+      { configPath },
+    )
+    expect(result.appConfig.output_formatter).toBe('jq')
+  })
+
+  it('should use config output formatter when no CLI flag', async () => {
+    fs.writeFileSync(configPath, 'output_formatter: jq\n')
+    const result = await runPreflight(['node', 'claude-composer'], {
+      configPath,
+    })
+    expect(result.appConfig.output_formatter).toBe('jq')
+  })
+
+  it('should remove formatter with --no-output-formatter', async () => {
+    fs.writeFileSync(configPath, 'output_formatter: jq\n')
+    const result = await runPreflight(
+      ['node', 'claude-composer', '--no-output-formatter'],
+      { configPath },
+    )
+    expect(result.appConfig.output_formatter).toBeUndefined()
+  })
+})

pr_title: Add support for querying default pool metrics
issue:
#### Issue #335: Finch PoolManager times out when starting pools with `start_pool_metrics` enabled

For a system with high activity, we suddenly started facing this error:

```
error: ** (exit) exited in: GenServer.call(App.Finch.PoolManager, {:start_pools, {:https, "**redacted host**", 443}}, 5000)
    ** (EXIT) time out
```

After consideration, we tried disabling the `start_pool_metrics` option, and that has solved the issue.

Now, I hypothesize that `:persistent_term.put(key, fun.(current))` is the culprit, as it tries to update a persistent term that already exists. A better solution would be to store the metrics on the PoolManager's GenServer state or an ETS.


We are running Finch from the master branch on commit [6d1d6f1](https://github.com/sneako/finch/commit/6d1d6f167086c2d4d622e51c2e296f8f5ca6b24f), with Elixir `1.18.4` and Erlang `27.3`

pr_title: Fix TypeError when tracking usage with Anthropic models returning Pydantic objects
issue:
#### Issue #8965: [Bug] `TypeError` when using `track_usage()` with Anthropic models that return `CacheCreation` objects

### What happened?

## Summary
The `UsageTracker` crashes with a `TypeError` when tracking usage for Anthropic models that use prompt caching. Anthropic's API returns `CacheCreation` Pydantic model objects in the usage data, but DSPy's `_merge_usage_entries()` attempts to add these objects arithmetically, which fails.

## Expected Behavior
Usage tracking should work correctly with all LM providers, including Anthropic models with prompt caching enabled. The tracker should either:
- Skip or ignore non-numeric fields
- Convert Pydantic objects to their numeric values
- Handle these objects gracefully in some other way

## Actual Behavior
When calling `tracker.get_total_tokens()` after making multiple API calls to Anthropic with caching enabled, a `TypeError` is raised:

```bash
$ DSPY_CACHEDIR=./ignored/dspycache_$(date +%s).cache uv run --prerelease=allow repro_dspy_cache_bug.py

   ERROR: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'CacheCreationTokenDetails' and 'CacheCreationTokenDetails'

============================================================
✗ FAILED: Bug reproduced!
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/ndr/coding/github/stanfordnlp/dspy/repro_dspy_cache_bug.py", line 74, in <module>
    asyncio.run(main())
    ~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/homebrew/Cellar/python@3.13/3.13.5/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.13/lib/python3.13/asyncio/runners.py", line 195, in run
    return runner.run(main)
           ~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^
  File "/opt/homebrew/Cellar/python@3.13/3.13.5/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.13/lib/python3.13/asyncio/runners.py", line 118, in run
    return self._loop.run_until_complete(task)
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^
  File "/opt/homebrew/Cellar/python@3.13/3.13.5/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.13/lib/python3.13/asyncio/base_events.py", line 725, in run_until_complete
    return future.result()
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^
  File "/Users/ndr/coding/github/stanfordnlp/dspy/repro_dspy_cache_bug.py", line 62, in main
    total_usage = tracker.get_total_tokens()
  File "/Users/ndr/coding/github/stanfordnlp/dspy/dspy/utils/usage_tracker.py", line 58, in get_total_tokens
    total_usage = self._merge_usage_entries(total_usage, usage_entry)
  File "/Users/ndr/coding/github/stanfordnlp/dspy/dspy/utils/usage_tracker.py", line 42, in _merge_usage_entries
    result[k] = self._merge_usage_entries(current_v, v)
                ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/Users/ndr/coding/github/stanfordnlp/dspy/dspy/utils/usage_tracker.py", line 44, in _merge_usage_entries
    result[k] = (current_v or 0) + (v or 0)
                ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'CacheCreationTokenDetails' and 'CacheCreationTokenDetails'

```

## Root Cause
The bug seems to be in [`dspy/utils/usage_tracker.py:44`](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/main/dspy/utils/usage_tracker.py#L44):

```python
result[k] = (current_v or 0) + (v or 0)
```

This line assumes all usage values are numeric (int/float), but Anthropic's API returns structured objects like:

```python
Usage(
    input_tokens=100,
    output_tokens=50,
    cache_creation_input_tokens=CacheCreation(ephemeral_1h_input_tokens=1024, ephemeral_5m_input_tokens=512),
    cache_read_input_tokens=None
)
```

When merging usage from multiple API calls, the code tries to add two `CacheCreation` objects together, which fails because Pydantic models don't support addition.

## Steps to Reproduce

I've included a standalone reproduction script (`repro_dspy_cache_bug.py`) that demonstrates the issue. To run it:

```bash
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your_key_here DSPY_CACHEDIR=./cache uv run --prerelease=allow repro_dspy_cache_bug.py
```


## Additional Context
- The bug only manifests when:
  1. Using Anthropic models (Claude)
  2. Making 2+ API calls within a `track_usage()` context
  3. The API returns `CacheCreation` objects (when caching is used)
- First call doesn't crash (nothing to merge)
- OpenAI and other providers that return only numeric usage values are unaffected

## Proposed Solution
The `_merge_usage_entries()` method should detect non-numeric values and handle them appropriately. Possible approaches:
1. Check if values support addition before attempting it
2. Convert Pydantic models to dicts before merging
3. Store non-numeric values in a way that doesn't require arithmetic operations

I can submit a PR with a fix if helpful!




### Steps to reproduce

Run the following with:

`DSPY_CACHEDIR=./dspycache_$(date +%s).cache uv run --prerelease=allow repro_dspy_cache_bug.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --prerelease=allow
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.12"
# dependencies = [
#     "dspy==3.0.4b1",
#     "anthropic",
# ]
# ///
"""
Reproduces DSPy usage tracker bug with Anthropic prompt caching.

When using cache=True with Anthropic models, the API returns a CacheCreation object
in the usage data. DSPy's usage tracker tries to add these objects like numbers,
causing: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'CacheCreation' and 'CacheCreation'

The bug is in dspy/utils/usage_tracker.py:44 where it assumes all values are numeric.

Run with: uv run repro_dspy_cache_bug.py
Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable.

run with:
DSPY_CACHEDIR=./ignored_dspycache_$(date +%s).cache uv run --prerelease=allow repro_dspy_cache_bug.py

A second run with the same cache will succeed even if the first failed.
"""

import asyncio
import os

import dspy
from dspy.utils.usage_tracker import track_usage


async def main() -> None:
    # Verify API key is set
    if not os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"):
        raise ValueError("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable must be set")

    # Create LM with a large system prompt to trigger caching
    # Anthropic only caches content blocks >= 1024 tokens
    lm = dspy.LM(
        model="claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929",
        #model = "gpt-4o-mini" # <--- with this model the script succeeds
        cache=True,
        max_tokens=1000,
    )

    # Use track_usage context manager to trigger the bug


    with track_usage() as tracker:
        with dspy.context(lm=lm):
            predictor = dspy.Predict("question -> answer")

            # Just make 2 calls - that's all we need!
            await predictor.acall(question="What is 2+2?")
            # So commenting this line makes the script succeed
            await predictor.acall(question="What is 3+3?")

        # The bug happens HERE when merging usage with cache_creation objects
        try:
            total_usage = tracker.get_total_tokens()
            print(f"   Total usage: {total_usage}")
            print("\n" + "=" * 60)
            print("✓ SUCCESS: Bug is fixed! The script completed without errors.")
        except TypeError as e:
            print(f"\n   ERROR: {e}")
            print("\n" + "=" * 60)
            print("✗ FAILED: Bug reproduced!")
            raise


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### DSPy version

3.0.4b1

issue:
#### Issue #44549: [Bug]: Bug Report: OpenClaw 2026.3.11 breaks all Tool Execution for `moonshotai/kimi-k2.5` via `openai-completions`

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Summary

When using moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 (via NVIDIA NIM, api: openai-completions) as the primary agent in OpenClaw 2026.3.11, the agent completely fails to parse and execute any tools (including read, exec, web_search, etc.).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 as the primary model using NVIDIA NIM (integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1) with api: openai-completions.
2. 2. Send a prompt that requires tool execution: openclaw agent --message "use the read tool to read MEMORY.md".
3. 3. The agent fails to use the tool, and the CLI/logs show hallucinated raw function strings instead of standard OpenAI tool schemas.

### Expected behavior

The agent should successfully parse the tool schema and invoke the tool, as it did reliably in v2026.2.25. The complex schema expansions introduced in recent 2026.3.x updates seem to instantly break Kimi's ability to format tool calls, returning raw identifiers.

### Actual behavior

Instead of correctly invoking the tool payload, Kimi leaks raw, hallucinatory tokens directly into the response (e.g. functionsweb_search53b7ac... or functionsessions_spawn...), causing the Gateway to reject the attempt with an error like Tool unknown not found.

### OpenClaw version

2026.3.11

### Operating system

Linux

### Install method

npm global

### Model

nvidia-kimi/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> NVIDIA NIM

### Config file / key location

~/.openclaw/openclaw.json

### Additional provider/model setup details

Environment:
- OS: Linux
- - Model: nvidia-kimi/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5
- - - Last known working version: 2026.2.25
Additional Context:
The bug 400 This model only supports single tool-calls at once! originally reported and supposedly fixed by PR #39356 is a symptom of this. Even when the Gateway blocks parallel tool calls, Kimi physically cannot understand the new bloated tool schemas (specifically sessions_spawn and the overall schema payload) in v3.11, causing the payload generation to crash natively on the LLM side. We had to forcefully downgrade to 2026.2.25 to restore productivity.

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

```shell

```

### Impact and severity

Affected: All users using Kimi-k2.5 via NVIDIA NIM with tool use.
Severity: High (completely blocks tool use/agent functionality).
Frequency: 100% repro on versions 2026.3.7+.
Consequence: Agent cannot perform tasks requiring tools, hallucinates tool calls instead.

### Additional information

#### Issue #55942: [Bug]: NVIDIA NIM Kimi 2.5 tool execution completely broken in OpenClaw > 2026.2.25

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

# Regression: NVIDIA NIM Kimi 2.5 tool execution completely broken in OpenClaw > 2026.2.25

**Issue Type:** Bug (Regression)  
**Affected Version:** OpenClaw > 2026.2.25 (2026.3.7–2026.3.24)  
**Last Working Version:** 2026.2.25  
**Component:** Agents / OpenAI-compatible providers  
**Provider:** NVIDIA NIM (`moonshotai/kimi-k2.5`)  

## Summary

Kimi 2.5 via NVIDIA NIM provider fails to execute **any** tool calls in OpenClaw versions after 2026.2.25. The model hallucinates tool call attempts which OpenClaw rejects with `"Tool not found"` errors, creating an infinite failure loop. While subagents with simple contexts work, main sessions with complex history trigger immediate failure.

## Symptoms

### Observed Failure Pattern
```
{"type":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_auto_1","toolName":"unknown","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Tool  not found"}]}
```

### User Experience
1. **Agent appears to be reasoning** (thinking blocks visible)
2. **Attempts to call tools** but outputs malformed tool calls
3. **OpenClaw rejects** with `"Tool not found"` error
4. **Agent retries** thinking it needs to fix something → infinite loop
5. **No actual tool execution** occurs

### Session Log Example (2026-03-27)
```
16:10:58 Kimi: "The user wants me to search ..."
16:10:58 OpenClaw: "Tool  not found"
16:11:04 Kimi: "Let me use the  access pattern from TOOLS..."
16:11:04 OpenClaw: "Tool  not found"
[Repeats 10+ times with different reasoning]
```

## Root Cause Analysis

### 1. Tool Schema Complexity (Primary Issue)
**PR #44888** ("compact Kimi tool schemas for openai-completions") attempts to address this but is **insufficient**:
- Strips `$defs`, `definitions`, `description`, `title`, `examples` for Kimi
- **BUT** Kimi still cannot parse remaining schema complexity
- **Result:** Kimi hallucinates tool calls → OpenClaw rejects → infinite failure

### 2. Message Format Mismatch (Secondary Issue)  
**PR #50152** ("normalize text-only content arrays to strings for OpenAI-compatible providers") helps but doesn't fix tool execution:
- Fixes Anthropic-style arrays → OpenAI strings for NVIDIA NIM
- **BUT** tool schema failures occur before message format issues

### 3. Configuration Drift
- **2026.2.25:** Simple tool schemas, string-only message content
- **2026.3.7+:** Complex schemas (`$defs`, nested objects), array-formatted content
- **Result:** Kimi's parser overwhelmed by schema bloat

## Technical Details

### Working vs Broken Tool Call Format

**Other LLM (Working):**
```json
{
  "type": "toolCall",
  "id": "call_2bb34a49b9964ba396b90a88", 
  "name": "read",
  "arguments": {"path": "SOUL.md"}
}
```

**Kimi 2.5 (Broken):**
- Hallucinates/invalid tool call format
- Receives `"Tool not found"` response
- No proper JSON schema compliance

### Why Subagents Work But Main Session Fails
- **Subagents:** Isolated, simpler context, fewer tools in schema
- **Main session:** Complex history, full tool schema, accumulated context
- **Kimi limitation:** Can't handle schema complexity beyond threshold

## Related Issues & PRs

### Already Identified (Incomplete Fixes)
1. **#44549** (2026-03-13): "OpenClaw 2026.3.11 breaks all Tool Execution for `moonshotai/kimi-k2.5`"
   - **Summary:** Kimi 2.5 completely fails to parse and execute any tools
   - **Last working:** 2026.2.25
   - **Status:** Partially addressed by PR #44888 (insufficient)

2. **#50107** (2026-03-19): "NVIDIA Provider Sends Anthropic-Style Message Format"
   - **Root cause:** OpenClaw sends arrays, NVIDIA NIM expects strings
   - **Fix:** PR #50152 (message normalization)

3. **#44888** (2026-03-13): "compact Kimi tool schemas for openai-completions"
   - **Attempt:** Strip noisy schema keys for Kimi
   - **Result:** Insufficient - Kimi still fails

4. **#50152** (2026-03-19): "normalize text-only content arrays to strings"
   - **Fix:** Anthropic arrays → OpenAI strings for NVIDIA NIM
   - **Limitation:** Doesn't address tool schema issues

## Testing Methodology

### Confirmed Working
- **Direct API calls:** `curl` to NVIDIA NIM API works
- **Subagents with simple tasks:** `read` tool works in isolation  
- **Authentication:** API key valid, provider configured correctly

### Confirmed Broken
- **Main session tool calls:** Any tool execution fails
- **Complex tool schemas:** `exec`, `web_fetch`, etc.
- **Messages with history:** Context > ~5k tokens triggers failure

## Proposed Solutions

### Option 1: Aggressive Schema Simplification (Recommended)
Extend PR #44888 with **more aggressive compaction**:
- Strip **ALL** optional fields for Kimi (`additionalProperties`, `pattern`, `enum`, `const`)
- Convert complex schemas to simple type declarations (`string`, `number`, `boolean`)
- Implement Kimi-specific schema transformer in `clean-for-kimi.ts`

### Option 2: Tool Call Format Fallback
When Kimi fails schema parsing:
- Fallback to **string-only tool descriptions** (ChatGPT-style function calling)
- Let Kimi output `{"name": "tool", "arguments": "string"}` format
- Parse string arguments server-side

### Option 3: NVIDIA NIM Provider-Specific Handling
- Add `provider === "nvidia" && modelId.includes("kimi")` special case
- Ultra-minimal tool schemas for Kimi-only
- Bypass normal schema validation for Kimi

### Option 4: Client-Side Workaround
Users can:
1. **Downgrade** to OpenClaw 2026.2.25
2. **Avoid Kimi** for main sessions (use subagents only)
3. **Use alternative models**

## Reproduction Steps

1. **Setup:** OpenClaw 2026.3.24, NVIDIA NIM provider configured
2. **Switch model:** `/model nvidia/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5`

- **Regression from working state** (2026.2.25)
- **Blocks users** relying on Kimi for reasoning tasks

### Affected Users
- Anyone using NVIDIA NIM Kimi 2.5 with OpenClaw > 2026.2.25
- Particularly affects users with complex tool requirements
- Workarounds limited (subagents only)

This is a **release-blocking regression**:

pr_title: fix: Ensure tags values are strings
issue:
#### Issue #4391: Ensure tag values are strings

[Tag values must be strings](https://develop.sentry.dev/sdk/data-model/event-payloads/span/); however, the Python SDK's methods for setting tags (`set_tag` on the `Scope`, on `Span`, and perhaps elsewhere) are defined as taking type `Any` for the value, and we do not convert the value to a string before setting the tag. 

While this appears to not be a problem for most users (likely our transport handles non-string-valued tags), it becomes a problem for users who wish to serialize the envelopes to send them with another service, like Sentry CLI. Since our spec requires tags to have string values, other services, in particular Sentry CLI, will refuse to accept envelopes created by the Python SDK when they contain a tag with a non-string value. See for example the issue [CLI-80](https://linear.app/getsentry/issue/CLI-80/using-send-envelope-error-with-types-invalid-type-boolean-false) (GitHub getsentry/sentry-cli#2505), which is caused by the Python SDK setting a non-string-valued tag.

My proposed solution is to modify all of our `set_tag` functions to convert all values to strings before setting them on the tag. If the conversion fails, we don't set the tag.

+import pytest
+import sentry_sdk
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("key", "value", "expected"),
+    [
+        ("int", 123, "123"),
+        ("float", 123.456, "123.456"),
+        ("bool_true", True, "True"),
+        ("bool_false", False, "False"),
+        ("list", [1, 2, 3], "(1, 2, 3)"),
+        ("dict", {"key": "value"}, '{"key": "value"}'),
+        ("already_string", "test", "test"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_span_set_tag_converts_to_string(
+    sentry_init, capture_events, key, value, expected
+):
+    """Test that Span.set_tag converts various types to strings."""
+    sentry_init(traces_sample_rate=1.0)
+    events = capture_events()
+
+    with sentry_sdk.start_span() as span:
+        span.set_tag(key, value)
+
+    (event,) = events
+
+    assert event["tags"][key] == expected, f"Tag {key} was not converted properly"
+
+

+

+    # This needs to be a subclass of something that otel supports as an

+    class BadObject(int):
+        def __str__(self):
+            raise NotImplementedError("Cannot convert to string")
+
+        def __repr__(self):
+            return "BadObject()"
+
+    with sentry_sdk.start_span() as span:
+        span.set_tag("bad_object", BadObject())
+
+    (event,) = events
+
+    assert event["tags"]["bad_object"] == "BadObject()"
+
+
+def test_span_set_tag_handles_broken_repr(sentry_init, capture_events):
+    """Test that Span.set_tag handles objects with broken __str__ and __repr__."""
+    sentry_init(traces_sample_rate=1.0)
+    events = capture_events()
+
+    # Create an object that raises exceptions for both __str__ and __repr__
+    class BadObject(int):
+        def __str__(self):
+            raise NotImplementedError("Cannot convert to string")
+
+        def __repr__(self):
+            raise NotImplementedError("Cannot get representation")
+
+    bad_obj = BadObject()
+
+    # This should not raise an exception
+    with sentry_sdk.start_span() as span:
+        span.set_tag("bad_object", bad_obj)
+
+    # The tag should be set to a fallback value
+    (event,) = events
+
+    assert event["tags"]["bad_object"] == "<broken repr>"

pr_title: Agents: dedupe repeated tool call ids
issue:
#### Issue #42116: Discord bot HTTP 400: tool call id write:202 is duplicated

## Bug Report: Discord bot returns HTTP 400 - "tool call id write:202 is duplicated"

### Description
When using Discord bot functionality, the bot fails to respond to interactions (button clicks, slash commands) with the error:
```
HTTP 400: Invalid request: tool call id write:202 is duplicated
```

### Environment
- **OpenClaw Version**: 2026.3.8 (3caab92)
- **OS**: macOS (Darwin 25.4.0 arm64)
- **Node.js**: v24.12.0
- **Model Provider**: Moonshot (kimi-k2.5)

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure Discord bot with valid token
2. Start OpenClaw Gateway
3. Trigger a Discord interaction (button click or slash command)
4. Observe the error in logs

### Expected Behavior
Discord bot should respond to interactions without errors.

### Actual Behavior
The bot fails with HTTP 400 error from Moonshot API:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Invalid request: tool call id write:202 is duplicated",
    "type": "invalid_request_error"
  }
}
```

### Root Cause Analysis

pr_title: fix: refresh skillsSnapshot when snapshotVersion changes
issue:
#### Issue #47832: skillsSnapshot not refreshed on /new or gateway restart for existing sessions

## Bug Description

`skillsSnapshot` in `sessions.json` is never refreshed for existing sessions, even after `/new` command or gateway restart. Only truly new sessions (first-ever creation) get a fresh skill scan.

## Root Cause

In `agent-*.js` (session resolution):

```js
const isNewSession = !fresh && !opts.sessionId;
const needsSkillsSnapshot = isNewSession || !sessionEntry?.skillsSnapshot;
```

When `/new` is used, it passes a new `opts.sessionId`, making `isNewSession = false`. Since the session already has a `skillsSnapshot` field, `needsSkillsSnapshot` evaluates to `false` — the old snapshot is reused.

There is a `snapshotVersion` field computed by `getSkillsSnapshotVersion()`, but it's never compared against the existing snapshot's version to detect staleness.

## Expected Behavior

`needsSkillsSnapshot` should also be `true` when:
1. `/new` creates a new session (new sessionId)
2. The `snapshotVersion` has changed since the snapshot was taken (skills added/removed)

Suggested fix:
```js
const needsSkillsSnapshot = isNewSession 
  || !sessionEntry?.skillsSnapshot
  || sessionEntry.skillsSnapshot.snapshotVersion !== skillsSnapshotVersion;
```

## Impact

- Users add a custom skill to `~/.openclaw/skills/`, but existing channels never see it
- `/new` doesn't help — users expect it to reset everything including available skills
- Gateway restart doesn't help either — `sessions.json` persists the stale snapshot
- **Only workaround**: manually edit `sessions.json` to inject missing skills or delete the `skillsSnapshot` field

## Reproduction

1. Create a session in a channel (e.g., group chat) — skills are snapshotted
2. Add a new skill to `~/.openclaw/skills/` (e.g., `sonar-search`)
3. Restart gateway (`launchctl kickstart -k`)
4. Use `/new` in that channel
5. The new skill is still missing from the agent's available skills

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.3.13
- macOS Darwin 24.6.0

pr_title: Support enharmonic spellings and double accidentals
issue:
#### Issue #40: Tone 'Cb' not found in system

Will expand on this later. But the issue is that "Cb" has a legal interpretation, well two interpretations really, a naïve one that would be Tone("Cb") == Tone("B"), and one where Cb~=B (but not quite identical)

---

#### Issue #41: Tones with more than 1 modifier sustained or flat modifier.

Tones like Cbb have a legal representation. Similarly to #40, there's two interpretations (depends on tuning used), but starting with the naïve interpretation, Cbb is just Bb (And similarly, Dbb would be C) (enharmonicness).


Double sustained (less frequently double flats) occurs often when the key signature contains accidentals, and then a specific note adds an accidental on top of that.

The oldest examples of double sharps I can find are Bach's Well Tempered Clavier (Prelude 3, Book 1), notated as a simple x. Modern double sharps are more common, one example I can find is Ravel's Ondine (1st movement Gaspard de la nuit).

In terms of API design, I think that both double flat and double sharp are conceptually the duplication of the individual symbols, so in that sense it's safe, it would be safe, if a bit creative to interpret the repeated accidental. However in the case of double flats, the symbol is literally two flat symbols together, so there's no other way to write a double flat really.

For the case of double sharps, the unicode symbol is 𝄪 and it might make sense for .from_string to accept that as well, in addition to ##. (for good measure, if this unicode symbol is interpreted by the from_string constructor, we should check if there's a formal double flat symbol and accept that too, even if it probably won't be used). there must be for double flat is more literally closer

While we are at it, it's worth mentioning that the # symbol isn't really the sharp symbol, the actual symbol has a different angle, lacking horizontal lines: ♯ .  Pytheory currently doesn't accept that (or flat unicode symbols). So as it's stands, we pytheory is currently using approximations present in the ASCII character set. 

For cleanliness I think that having each accidental be represented by an ASCII approximation and it's unicode counterpart might make for good documentation and API design:

|ASCII|Unicode|
|----|----|
|#|♯|
|b|♭|
|## or x or X|𝄪|
|bb|𝄫|

#### Issue #291: Discussion: `SqliteTask`

I am currently working on a simple implementation of a `SqliteTask` for interacting with `sqlite3` databases.

What I'd like to support:
- executing single statements and returning the values of `fetchall()` (or some prespecified number of return rows)
- executing full sql scripts (either as a string or read from a file); note that if you execute a script only, there is nothing to return

My current sketch design idea:
```python
class SqliteTask(Task):
    def __init__(self, statement: str = None, 
                       script: str = None, db: str = ":memory:", 
                       return_rows: int = 0, **kwargs):
        ...
```
Moreover, if you provide _both_ `script` and `statement`, the `script` will be executed first and the `statement` last, in case it's a `SELECT` statement to query what just happened in the script.

I'm opening this issue for discussion in case this is overloading the task with too many parameters / options / possibilities.  I want to make sure it's still clear as a single `Task`.

**cc**: @jlowin @joshmeek

pr_title: fix(a11y): recognize role="application" as interactive + regression test for #48
issue:
#### Issue #49: a11y-no-noninteractive-tabindex should recognize role="application" as interactive ## Description The `a11y-no-noninteractive-tabindex` warning incorrectly flags elements with `tabindex="0"` when they have `role="application"`, which makes them semantically interactive. According to [WAI-ARIA](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.1/#application), `role="application"` declares a region as a web application rather than a web document, making it an interactive widget that should be focusable. ## Minimal Reproduction ```svelte
``` ## Current Behavior ``` Warning: A11y: Non-interactive elements like
should not have tabindex (a11y-no-noninteractive-tabindex) ``` ## Expected Behavior No warning, because `role="application"` makes the element interactive. ## Additional Context Other interactive roles that should also be recognized include: - `role="button"` - `role="link"` - `role="menuitem"` - `role="tab"` - `role="slider"` - `role="textbox"` - etc. The official `svelte-check` handles this correctly by not warning when an interactive role is present. ## Environment - svelte-check-rs version: latest - OS: macOS

 As a quick recap, the Airbyte Specification requires an Airbyte Source to support 4 distinct operations:
 
-1. `Spec` - The required configuration in order to interact with the underlying technical system e.g. database
-
-   information, authentication information etc.
-
-2. `Check` - Validate that the provided configuration is valid with sufficient permissions for one to perform all
-
-   required operations on the Source.
-
-3. `Discover` - Discover the Source's schema. This let users select what a subset of the data to sync. Useful
-
-   if users require only a subset of the data.
-
-4. `Read` - Perform the actual syncing process. Data is read from the Source, parsed into `AirbyteRecordMessage`s
-
-   and sent to the Airbyte Destination. Depending on how the Source is implemented, this sync can be incremental
-
-   or a full-refresh.
+| Operation | Description |
+| --- | --- |
+| `Spec` | The required configuration in order to interact with the underlying technical system e.g. database information, authentication information etc. |
+| `Check` | Validate that the provided configuration is valid with sufficient permissions for one to perform all required operations on the Source. |
+| `Discover` | Discover the Source's schema. This let users select what a subset of the data to sync. Useful if users require only a subset of the data. |
+| `Read` | Perform the actual syncing process. Data is read from the Source, parsed into `AirbyteRecordMessage`s and sent to the Airbyte Destination. Depending on how the Source is implemented, this sync can be incremental or a full-refresh. |

#### Issue #350: Security hardening: remediate aardvark/codex scanner findings

## Summary

An automated security scanner (aardvark/codex) opened 13 PRs (#337-#349) against the repository. After principal-engineer review, **11 were validated as legitimate** and **2 were rejected** (one as security theater, one as destructive). The original PRs were closed due to provenance issues and are being re-implemented cleanly in a single PR.

## Validated Findings

| PR | Severity | Title | Status |
|----|----------|-------|--------|
| #342 | Critical | L7 REST parser overread enables request smuggling | Implementing |
| #345 | Critical | OPA policy matches attacker-controlled cmdline paths | Implementing |
| #347 | Critical | Symlink following in read_write chown enables privilege escalation | Implementing |
| #338 | Critical | No application-layer auth in dual-auth/edge mode | Implementing |
| #337 | High | Missing process identity skips privilege dropping | Implementing |
| #339 | High | Forward proxy bypasses L7 method/path enforcement | Implementing |
| #340 | High | No validation on sandbox-discovered policy without baseline | Implementing |
| #341 | High | TLS secret volume readable by sandbox user (0644 default) | Implementing |
| #344 | High | Provider CRUD RPCs return plaintext credentials | Implementing |
| #346 | Low | drop_privileges no-op when process user unset (defense-in-depth, overlaps #337) | Implementing |
| #348 | Low | Server binds 0.0.0.0 by default (hardening) | Implementing |

## Rejected Findings

| PR | Reason |
|----|--------|
| #343 | Security theater: `x-sandbox-id` header is self-asserted with no cryptographic binding. Also breaks all existing callers since the sandbox client never sets the header. Needs redesign with per-sandbox certs or server-issued tokens. |
| #349 | Destructive: blocking AF_INET/AF_INET6 in proxy mode would break the proxy itself. Sandboxed processes must create inet sockets to reach the proxy at 10.200.0.1:3128. Network isolation is already enforced by the network namespace + iptables rules. |

## Agent Diagnostic

All 13 PRs were reviewed using the `review-security-issue` skill with `principal-engineer-reviewer` sub-agents. Each finding was traced through the codebase to validate or refute the claimed vulnerability, assess severity, and evaluate the proposed fix.

issue:
#### Issue #3588: CanvasCreated event not published to RabbitMQ when using Health Check Monitor quick start on a fresh organization

## Summary

When starting a fresh new organization and clicking the `Health Check Monitor` quick start, the expected `CanvasCreated` message is never published to RabbitMQ. The `Usage` section continues to show 0 canvases created, indicating the event is silently dropped or never emitted.

## Requested work

- Reproduce the issue by creating a brand-new organization and launching the `Health Check Monitor` quick start canvas.
- Investigate why the `CanvasCreated` event is not being published to RabbitMQ in this flow.
- Verify the canvas creation path (API → event bus) for quick-start templates, especially on organizations with no prior canvases.
- Ensure the `CanvasCreated` message is reliably published so that downstream consumers (including the usage/metrics tracker) reflect the correct canvas count.
- Add or extend integration/end-to-end tests covering quick-start canvas creation on a fresh organization to prevent regression.

## SuperPlane context

Canvases are the core workflow primitive in SuperPlane. The `CanvasCreated` event is expected to flow through the event bus (RabbitMQ) whenever a new canvas is instantiated — whether from scratch or via a quick-start template. If this event is missing, usage metrics are incorrect and any downstream triggers or integrations that depend on `CanvasCreated` will not fire.

## Notes

- This may be specific to the first canvas created in a new organization (empty-state edge case).
- Check whether other quick-start templates exhibit the same behavior or if it is isolated to `Health Check Monitor`.
- Verify that the canvas record is actually persisted in the database even though the event is not published — this would narrow the bug to the event-publishing layer rather than the creation logic itself.

pr_title: Compaction Runner: wire post-compaction memory sync
issue:
#### Issue #19207: [Bug]: Compaction summarization does not preserve exact identifiers

### Summary

Default compaction summarization prompts preserve only file paths, function names, and error messages, causing other exact identifiers to be truncated or dropped.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a long OpenClaw session that includes exact identifiers (UUIDs, IPs, SHAs, container hashes, API paths with embedded IDs, connection strings, etc.).
2. Continue until auto-compaction runs (or trigger `/compact`).
3. Ask the model to recall exact identifiers that appeared in the compacted portion.
4. Observe that identifiers outside the preservation list are truncated, abbreviated, or missing — the model may hallucinate plausible but incorrect replacements.

### Expected behavior

Compaction summaries should preserve all exact identifiers verbatim, not only file paths, function names, and error messages.

### Actual behavior

Identifiers not explicitly named in the current preservation rule are truncated or omitted during summarization. After compaction, the model lacks a trustworthy source for those values and may hallucinate replacements, leading to wrong API calls, auth failures, and misconfigurations.

### OpenClaw version

2026.2.15

### Operating system

macOS 15.7.3 (24G419)

### Install method

npm global

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

```shell
- Prompt sources (in @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent):
-- SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT and UPDATE_SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT in dist/core/compaction/compaction.js
-- SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT in dist/core/compaction/utils.js
- Current prompt instruction explicitly says: “Preserve exact file paths, function names, and error messages.”
- This scope excludes other exact identifiers (UUIDs, IP/host/port values, SHAs, hashes, endpoint IDs, DB IDs, tokens/headers, pod names, build/version IDs, serial/MAC values, connection strings, URL-embedded IDs, and other precise identifiers).
- Real incident: an Outline collection UUID was compacted to prefix c7a1ae81; later the model hallucinated the missing UUID segments, causing a 403 Forbidden API response. The correct UUID had to be fetched again from Outline.
```

### Impact and severity

* **Affected users/systems/channels:** Any long-running OpenClaw workflow handling exact identifiers (infra, API development, database work, DevOps, and general technical sessions).
* **Severity (annoying, blocks workflow, data risk, etc.):** Data risk due to silent identifier corruption that drives incorrect operations.
* **Frequency (always/intermittent/edge case):** Always for compactions involving identifiers outside the narrow preservation list.
* **Consequence (missed messages, failed onboarding, extra cost, etc.):** Failed API/auth operations, wrong configurations, repeated refetching/revalidation, debugging overhead, and reduced trust in compacted context.

Examples of identifiers at risk include:

* UUIDs
* IP addresses, hostnames, and ports
* Git commit SHAs
* Docker container IDs and image hashes
* API endpoint paths containing IDs
* Database row IDs
* Session tokens
* Kubernetes pod names
* Version numbers and build IDs
* Serial numbers and MAC addresses
* Any other precise identifier that is not a file path, function name, or error message

### Additional information

- Related issues (separate but relevant feature requests for custom rules): #10479, #19148, #16092.
- Proposed fix direction: broaden default preservation text to explicitly include “exact identifiers, UUIDs, IP addresses, URLs, commit SHAs, connection strings, and all precise values.” This is a minimal, low-risk prompt-only change.
- `compaction.customInstructions` (tracked in #10479) can complement this by letting users add domain-specific preservation constraints.

#### Issue #3773: Update the Makefile to the BYO cluster with CNS + CNI

Update the makefile `https://github.com/Azure/azure-container-networking/tree/master/hack/aks` that should leverage the make file cmds mentioned below to create a byocni cluster based on the inputs.(Similar to the inputs passed to each Make cmd below). Make it universal and allow for other byocni scenarios. byocni cilium can be the default if the user does not specify another scenario.
Byocni cilium should be the default setup, but it should be configurable to create other types of clusters with the existing make targets.  
Steps to create:
1. [hackfile](https://github.com/Azure/azure-container-networking/blob/master/hack/aks/Makefile#L137) contains many helpful commands for cluster provisioning. For this scenario, we are using overlay-byocni-nokubeproxy-up. Example:
```AZCLI=az CLUSTER=byocni-cluster SUB=9b8218f9-902a-4d20-a65c-e98acec5362f make overlay-byocni-nokubeproxy-up
```
2. Deploy CNS to Cluster. The ACN repo contains the make command to deploy CNS to the cluster. Make sure the script has these variables configurable. Run this from root. Example:
```
    sudo -E env "PATH=$PATH" make test-load CNS_ONLY=true CNS_VERSION=v1.5.38 AZURE_IPAM_VERSION=v0.3.0 INSTALL_CNS=true INSTALL_OVERLAY=true CNS_IMAGE_REPO=MCR
```
3. This folder contains all of the [cilium manifests](https://github.com/Azure/azure-container-networking/tree/master/test/integration/manifests/cilium). You will need to deploy a particular version of cilium to the cluster. Make sure the variables are configurable For example,
```
    export DIR=<dir> # format 1.14
    export CILIUM_IMAGE_REGISTRY=acnpublic.azurecr.io # or mcr.microsoft.com/containernetworking if you need to use the published image
    export CILIUM_VERSION_TAG=<test-tag>
    kubectl apply -f test/integration/manifests/cilium/v${DIR}/cilium-config/cilium-config.yaml
    kubectl apply -f test/integration/manifests/cilium/v${DIR}/cilium-operator/files
    kubectl apply -f test/integration/manifests/cilium/v${DIR}/cilium-agent/files
    export IPV6_HP_BPF_VERSION=<bpf version> # Needed for dualstack
    envsubst '${CILIUM_VERSION_TAG},${CILIUM_IMAGE_REGISTRY},${IPV6_HP_BPF_VERSION}' < test/integration/manifests/cilium/v${DIR}/cilium-operator/templates/deployment.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
    envsubst '${CILIUM_VERSION_TAG},${CILIUM_IMAGE_REGISTRY},${IPV6_HP_BPF_VERSION}' < test/integration/manifests/cilium/v${DIR}/cilium-agent/templates/daemonset.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```
